pub fn authority_snapshot(&self) -> SchemaAuthoritySnapshot {
        let (primary_schema_id, primary_schema_version_id) = self
            .authoritative_schema_basis()
            .ok()
            .flatten()
            .map(|(schema_id, schema_version_id)| (Some(schema_id), Some(schema_version_id)))
            .unwrap_or((None, None));

        let entity_kinds = self
            .entity_kinds
            .iter()
            .map(|(kind_id, registration)| SchemaAuthorityKindSnapshot {
                kind_id: *kind_id,
                kind_name: registration.kind_name.clone(),
                schema_id: registration.schema_id.clone(),
                schema_version_id: registration.schema_version_id,
                aspect_plan_revision: registration.aspect_contract_declarations.plan_revision,
            })
            .collect();
        let relation_kinds = self
            .relation_kinds
            .iter()
            .map(|(kind_id, registration)| SchemaAuthorityRelationSnapshot {
                kind_id: *kind_id,
                kind_name: registration.kind_name.clone(),
                schema_id: registration.schema_id.clone(),
                schema_version_id: registration.schema_version_id,
                aspect_plan_revision: registration.aspect_contract_declarations.plan_revision,
                relation_integrity_plan_revision: derive_relation_integrity_plan_revision(
                    &registration.relation_integrity.endpoint_kind_contracts,
                    &registration.relation_integrity.cardinality_contracts,
                    &registration.relation_integrity.uniqueness_contracts,
                    &registration.relation_integrity.symmetry_contracts,
                    &registration
                        .relation_integrity
                        .endpoint_deletion_integrity_contracts,
                    &registration.relation_integrity.acyclicity_contracts,
                    &registration
                        .relation_integrity
                        .partition_isolation_contracts,
                    &registration
                        .relation_integrity
                        .connectivity_minimum_contracts,
                    registration.relation_integrity.aggregate_identity.as_ref(),
                ),
                cross_context_policy: registration.cross_context_policy,
                cascade_delete_policy: registration.cascade_delete_policy,
            })
            .collect();

        SchemaAuthoritySnapshot {
            content_formats: self.content_formats.snapshot(),
            primary_schema_id,
            primary_schema_version_id,
            entity_kinds,
            relation_kinds,
            derived_relations: self.derived_parts(),
            projected_member_domains: self.projected_domain_parts(),
        }
    }

Ordinary checkpoint restore has the same original-request option:
`host::application_installation::in_memory_rostered_program_from_checkpoint_in_advancement`
takes that bootstrap phase first, followed by the validated program, roster,
declaration, configuration, build identity, unchanged World limits and checkpoint.
It reconstructs through the ordinary restore core and accepts no seed or transition
callback. Use a separately funded opening request for a large recovered population;
its allowance does not increase later World business calls. Default ordinary
checkpoint restoration continues to open from the World request policy.

When installation belongs to an already admitted execution attempt, borrow its
`ExecutionRequest` through `host::application_contribution::with_bootstrap_advancement_from_request`
and pass the resulting phase to
`host::application_installation::in_memory_rostered_program_from_checkpoint_with_transition_in_advancement`.
This variant takes the existing transition arguments with the phase first and a
required capture policy. It borrows the original cancellation/deadline and
remaining cumulative work through construction, roster admission, native transition,
final assembly and capture. Native nested scopes charge the original parent; they
do not renew its allowance. Capture is capped by the caller-named policy, which must
be `Execution(&lease)` for the funding lease itself or a lease descending from it,
for example a child with its own smaller memory limit; there is no default and no
silent inheritance. Entry checks that descent before any work or charge: a sibling,
a parent or another lineage's lease refuses with
`ExecutionDenied(ExecutionResource { NestedLeaseMisuse })`. A capture child that runs
out after the native ACK returns the acknowledged capsule with the child's own
refusal (`Policy { ancestor: 0 }`) for repair.
`SystemAllocation` and bare serial backing have no admitted capture allocation policy and refuse before
effects with `ExecutionDenied(ResourceEnvelopeMismatch)`, rather than falling back
to SystemAllocation. The ordinary convenience constructor retains its explicit
owned-request/policy contract. Its `Execution(&lease)` policy funds the whole
transition: the bootstrap runs on that lease, as if borrowed through
`with_bootstrap_advancement_from_request`, so the lease carries the transition's
work as well as the captured frame.

The lower Store Application `readmit_world` seam composes the same admitted
Native owner with privately constructed Bridge and the authored Signal owner.
Its first Relational-only durable lane requires an untouched InitialEmpty Signal
root and an uninstalled Bridge baseline. Their versioned owner recipes, the
exact Native predecessor and the program revision are mandatory World artifact
v3 fields. Graph equality, a source profile or an old process identifier cannot
readmit component authority. Native recovery, Signal seed admission, Bridge
baseline admission and World reconciliation retain that order.

The fresh Native-only Directory Host journey now opens the actual Home,
initializes once, reads seeded data, publishes an ordinary mutation through the
same World, and closes through the owning Home. A genuine retained runtime
clone produces a composition refusal after World seal; dropping that clone and
retrying the same close custody completes the close. Existing Directory startup
uses the same ordinary Home request and physical location. It admits the recorded
portable schema/program meaning, completion and activation through the recovered
World root without calling the initializer or replaying seed suppliers.

Fresh Memory and Directory startup publish the same bootstrap completion commit
after every seed batch and index build succeeds, before creating World genesis.
The record describes installed package/schema meaning, the terminal seed receipt
and counts; it grants no durable association to Memory. A refused Directory
completion keeps the accepted seeds and original Home in opening custody without
rerunning initialization. Development Homes with the retired completion format
refuse with a typed Query recovery outcome; opening performs no migration.

Ordinary reads after reopen use the selected published World basis, including
when independent Native history is newer. Actual recovered index definitions
and the generations needed at that basis are admitted before serving a request.
An exact old mutation key returns `RecoveredCommitted`, preserving the original
recorded receipt without rerunning the business handler. Inspect
`outcome.recovered_receipt()` for original Native meaning, old/new product
references, publication attempt, intent, outcome, emitted effects, exact output
settlement, dispatch outbox and aftermath causality. Every field comes from the
original owner artifacts. The recorded receipt carries no live output or
publication authority and does not reconstruct a Rust handler result. Query
fresh current state separately. A changed intent returns `IdempotencyIntentDrift`;
a foreign product affinity refuses at idempotency admission. Keep unresolved or
unpublished custody and follow its typed recovery route before trying again.
New keys receive identities beyond the actual durable outcome frontier.
Malformed, duplicate or invalid binding state returns owning opening refusal.
An exhausted outcome frontier refuses the new commit.

For retained reads, pass the recovered data to
`request.at_original_receipt(&phase, &receipt, maximum_history_work)` under a
fresh authorized request. This selects through the current owner's real history
and can refuse unavailable retained material. `at_recorded_commit` accepts the
Home-scoped commit coordinate. Neither method turns recorded data into live
publication or recovery authority. Owning source completion exposes recorded
evidence through `recorded_receipt()` and already-held live evidence through
`live_receipt()`; keep its publication and cleanup obligations until lawful close.

Treat `ProductPreparationPending` as original custody. Keep the returned
terminal and business key; duplicate requests must observe that custody rather
than invoke the handler again. `try_into_recovery()` is an explicit unbudgeted
handoff of the actual retained phase. A busy handoff returns the same terminal.
Inspect the returned record's actual `next_actions()`, using
`worth_query_host::facade::primary_graph::ProductUnpublishedNextAction`.

For a persistent live open, the canonical `RuntimeWorldRecoveryDenial` reports
`ReopenRequired` and the record permits exactly `[Inspect, ReopenRequired]`.
Preserve stable request/correlation data and end ownership of the current Home,
then reopen the same physical location under Store's new mutation lease for
recovered reconciliation. A close refusal keeps its actual recovery custody;
ordinary disposal is neither release nor successful close. The old lease blocks
concurrent open. Old recovery handles are incarnation-fenced, so obtain claims
from the newly readmitted Home. Do not loop live release, reconstruct the old
proposal, or resubmit the handler.
Zero observed effects are descriptive and do not issue a no-effect authority.
Reopen validates each recovered World open against its actual Native association
and original Query key/intent/affinity before admitting service. Untypable or
inconsistent original evidence still returns an owning typed opening refusal.
Retrying the original key returns distinct recovered `ProductUnpublished`
custody, with the original Native meaning and predecessor, and no reconstructed
Rust return value. Its `ContinueOriginalPublication` action is executed through
`continue_original_in_request` on the fresh recovery claim: it publishes the
original occurrence without handler or effect replay. Release first commits its
original durable disposition. Pending/refused outcomes retain the same owner.
A released effect-bearing original keeps its idempotency binding. Explicit
resolution returns `ReleasedOriginal` with the original Native meaning and
release provenance. It carries no application receipt or adoption authority.
An ordinary retry refuses with `OriginalEffectReleased` before the handler;
changed intent still reports drift. Only an actual no-effect release permits
fresh execution of that key. Memory release preserves the same terminal meaning
without claiming a durable World association.
A durable `Continued` disposition excludes release across every subsequent open. Persisted
workflow, outbox, inbound-completion and aftermath rows refuse cold service;
compiled workflow declarations alone remain allowed. Missing or incompatible
completion artifacts keep their existing origin and never regain initialization.

Directory startup also refuses before service if Store finds a retained entry
or unresolved publication in an unsupported transition, Signal or Query
obligation journal, or cannot inspect that journal. The opening refusal owns
the original Query preparation and Home. Consume its `close` operation to
release them through the actual lifecycle; a refusal continues to hold the
mutation lease. Matching program activation does not settle a pending Home
transition.

A terminal `ProductPreparationRefused` has no future publication or retry door.
Its business entry is released, while its opaque carrier can still own partial
successor reservations. Discard it to release those resources through ordinary
unbudgeted destruction before an otherwise resource-blocked fresh attempt.
Resource contention is distinct from a retained business key. Memory continues
to use its actual owner-specific recovery actions.

See [the Home composition capability](capability-index.md#compose-world-with-an-admitted-application-home)
for current refusals and lifecycle custody.

Store Application's `readmit_world` consumes the concrete Native-readmitted
Home and an `ApplicationWorldDefinition`. The private attachment injects the
same actual Native runtime into World and Bridge. The resulting
`WorldReadmittedApplicationHome::world()` borrows existing publication,
branch/history observation, inspection and recovery ports; only Home owns
World's lifecycle. Use that Home's `close` and retain its actual refusal or
recovery custody for retry. Accepted World journal tasks stay in the same
Home custody through physical teardown. Close stops and settles accepted work;
unsettled work refuses close. Terminal indeterminate evidence permits teardown
and reopen, while keeping runtime publication admission fenced.

This lower composition seam requires the actual Native recovery authority and
its complete associated-effect inventory. Failed admission returns
`WorldHomeReadmissionRefused`, retaining the same concrete Home, lease and World
slot; `into_home` explicitly cleans up refused component custody and returns
that Native-readmitted Home. Attached memory bootstrap, legacy publication and
branch mutation doors refuse before effects. Query's closed
`query_publication_home_binding(expected)` selector admits the actual live owner
and exact process identity, then checks its retained Home binding. Only genuine
memory ownership returns `None`; unavailable, foreign or inconsistent ownership
returns its typed refusal before any I/O. Publication still authenticates through
its original effectful preparation doors.
Live directory preparation abandonment retains its original World and Query
custody and offers `Inspect` plus `ReopenRequired`. Its live release/continuation
also returns `RuntimeWorldRecoveryDenial::ReopenRequired`; neither a zero effect
count nor an empty live inventory proves no effect. End current Home/process
ownership and reopen under Store's mutation lease. The closed pre-service D8
recipe supplies the actual Native recovery authority to World's complete
associated inventory admission before reconciliation, including empty World
journals. That authority checks its exact runtime; it is historical recovery
evidence, not a live publication fence. Recovered custody keeps its distinct
durable-before-live disposition operations. Query admits its actual original
key/intent/affinity before service; retry returns distinct recovered
`ProductUnpublished` custody. Inspect its original Native meaning and predecessor,
then use the fresh recovery claim's `continue_original_in_request` for the
original occurrence, or the existing release route for durable release. Neither
runs the handler again. Pending/refused outcomes retain that same owner. A
committed `Continued` permits original continuation and forbids release after
reopen; it is never appended twice.

World lifecycle `close(request, &actual_owner)` uses the caller's original request, nonwaiting
admission, and the existing publication frontier. Before sealing, contention or
interruption preserves Open. After sealing, the same retained task owns each
extracted head, its populated history slot, retirement phases and report;
interruption preserves Closing. Ordinary weak ports stay unavailable while the
close-only weak port can retry that same task. Its authentic same-owner borrow
keeps the actual root alive through return; a foreign owner is refused without
weak upgrade or root cloning. Unresolved business, pending
bootstrap and owner-created component retirement custody refuse before sealing.
This minimum also refuses Directory custody without a qualified durable handoff;
it does not claim full request-aware Home or Native snapshot cleanup.

The consuming `seal_world` retains the actual World close report and advances
the same World-owned result cleanup before dropping World. Initialization uses
original-request checks and trylocked constant-size Closed/catalog admission.
Each cleanup advance visits one sealed history slot or advances Native's genuine
original-result retirement task with the actual Home Native owner borrowed.
Busy, stop, Native refusal and observer loss retain the same cursor, result and
original release-cell custody; counts describe observed Native Complete outcomes.
Recovered publication capabilities never become synthetic live result tasks.
Final World/Bridge/Native destruction, materialized Native cache custody and cold
capability retirement retain their separate contracts; this is not full Home D11. A refused seal
retries through `try_seal_world`. Host can then release its Query observations
before `finish_close` attempts Native teardown. Shared conditional assembly
custody returns `WorldCompositionRetained` in the same Home recovery object;
retry uses actual ownership admission and runs conditional cleanup outside its
assembly lock. A sealed World never resumes Serving.
`publication_port().begin_durable_bootstrap_root(request, creation, native_basis,
signal_basis)` validates the actual current Signal owner and supplies the same
private Bridge's baseline. Its retained bootstrap can be advanced through
`advance_durable_bootstrap_root(request)`. The existing bootstrap state keeps the
original pre-install history, pins and branch cell across pending calls. World
artifact v3 requires Native's explicit recorded component, Signal's owner-proven
InitialEmpty recipe, Bridge's versioned registered-source baseline and the actual
program revision; v1/v2 and missing seed fields refuse. General authored Signal
or installed Bridge state refuses before this narrow bootstrap. Root installation follows the actual
sealed journal acknowledgement. The filesystem Home court covers this bootstrap,
ordinary Relational-only publication and exact World-owned result snapshot
cleanup. Undelivered publication refuses Home close before teardown; recover
its original delivery through `recovery_port().recover_performed` and consume it
before retrying. Independent Native reads retain their own close obligations.

World's durable open retains its original identities and one Native preparation,
and its prepared wrapper executes through `execute_durable_without_signal`.
The original occurrence backing is admitted before Native effects, then filled
only with the original settled receipt, position and artifact digest. Actual
journal selection authorizes the same cell's live CAS; pending retains the
original ready custody and capacities. Attached checkpoint
refuses `WorldSectionRequired`; close reports that checkpoint failure. Native-only
reopened Home checkpoint also refuses before capture when actual World journal
heads exist. This presence check grants no World proof from empty streams;
already-accepted checkpoint recovery still settles and actually acknowledges
its original task before Native close admission.

Cold readmission supports one initial product branch and its ordinary
Relational-only occurrence chain. Each occurrence admits its exact original
Native predecessor and successor from actual recovery; later Native advancement
does not replace either historical root. World validates the actual journal
positions, payload digests, association and recorded Native evidence, restores
the original durable identities and head generations, and issues fresh local
owner custody. `observation_port().readmitted_publication` takes a Foundational
`DurableCompositeCommitIdentity` as lookup data and returns an owning protected
view of that original occurrence and Native semantic result. It exposes no live
`CommitResult`, snapshot, timing or `Performed` delivery; Native semantics do not
reconstruct arbitrary application return values. Native source-backed recovery
also reconstructs the exact predecessor and unpublished effect;
`inspection_port().recovery_page` exposes a Recovered
row, `recovery_port().inspect_recovered_effects` claims its original identities,
and `release_recovered_effects` durably records release before dropping the real
Native capability. Pending or refused release returns the same custody.
Released artifacts require explicit no-effect evidence or the complete original
Native receipt, position and digest, checked against Native's actual inventory
on reopen. The real filesystem child-process court kills after Native durability
before the World occurrence, reopens and releases the original custody, then
reopens with the same unmoved product head. The ordinary occurrence filesystem
court additionally publishes twice, advances Native again, closes, reopens both
historical semantic results and the original product head, then reopens again.
Its bounded history-capacity control retains the actual partial catalog,
admitted Native capabilities and same Home lease until explicit cleanup. The
existing kill child also covers a later unpublished Native effect whose exact
World predecessor is generation 2; release and second reopen preserve that head.
Multiple-branch readmission, recovered continuation, general Signal/Bridge state, Host retry and World
checkpoint coverage remain required for phase completion.
See [Milestone 3](../plans/database-foundation/milestone-3.md)
and the owning [Home attachment](../workspaces/worth-store/crates/worth-store-application/src/world_section/readmission.rs).
